stories.headline: Garment wage protests shut factories as government forms new wage board
stories.summary: Garment workers demanding a Tk 30,000 minimum monthly wage shut 177 factories in Savar and Ashulia on 1 November, while BGMEA reported disruptions at 529 factories across Dhaka, Gazipur, Mymensingh and Savar-Ashulia, with 987,190 workers walking out. The government formed a six-member wage board the same day, chaired by Senior District Judge Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, but protests, road blockades and clashes with police continued in Mirpur and Gazipur.
stories.why_it_matters: The garment sector earns about 80 percent of Bangladesh's export income, so a wage settlement affects exports, inflation, labour relations and the budget — all core BCS/Bank topics.
stories.exam_facts: Demand: Tk 30,000 minimum monthly wage; 177 factories shut in Savar-Ashulia; 529 factories disrupted, 987,190 workers walked out (BGMEA); six-member wage board formed 1 November, chairman Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman; workers also demand an end to blacklisting and reinstatement of dismissed workers.
stories.exam_relevance: High — RMG, labour law, wage board, exports.
stories.key_people: Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, chairman of the wage board; Ariful Haque Choudhury, Labour and Employment Minister; Babul Akhter, BGIWF general secretary.
stories.figures: Tk 30,000 demanded minimum wage; 177 factories shut; 529 factories disrupted; 987,190 workers walked out; six-member wage board.

stories.headline: HSC pass rate falls to 51.62 percent, lowest in 22 years
stories.summary: The HSC pass rate fell to 51.62 percent, its lowest in 22 years, down from 57.12 percent last year, and GPA-5 achievers dropped by 27,271 to 35,948. Alim pass rates fell to 61.07 percent and technical to 49.43 percent, both two-decade lows. Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon blamed learning gaps, teacher shortages and weak classroom teaching, and said special exams for students failing one or two subjects will be held within two months.
stories.why_it_matters: Education outcomes and the reasons behind them are standard BCS/Bank questions; the figures show a sharp, measurable deterioration across all boards.
stories.exam_facts: HSC pass rate 51.62 percent (22-year low), down from 57.12 percent; GPA-5: 35,948, down 27,271 from 63,219; zero-pass institutions up to 181; Alim 61.07 percent, technical 49.43 percent; re-scrutiny applications 1-7 November; special exams within two months for students failing one or two subjects.
stories.exam_relevance: High — education policy, HSC, BANBEIS data.
stories.key_people: ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, Education Minister; Prof Khondaker Mohammad Sadequr Rahman, chairman, Bangladesh Madrasah Education Board.
stories.figures: 51.62 percent HSC pass rate; 35,948 GPA-5 (down 27,271); 181 zero-pass institutions; Alim 61.07 percent; technical 49.43 percent; 86,832 unsuccessful Alim/technical candidates.

stories.headline: Exports rise 6 percent to $17 billion in July-October
stories.summary: Bangladesh's exports grew 6 percent year-on-year to $17 billion in July-October, driven by garments: knitwear rose 7 percent to $7.71 billion and woven garments 4.8 percent to $6 billion, together about 80 percent of exports. Jute goods rose 23.8 percent and chemical products 27.3 percent, but agricultural exports fell 13.5 percent and frozen fish 10.9 percent, according to Bangladesh Bank data.
stories.why_it_matters: Export composition and growth are directly askable in BCS/Bank economics and trade questions, and the sector split shows where the growth comes from.
stories.exam_facts: Exports July-October: $17 billion, up 6 percent year-on-year; knitwear $7.71 billion (up 7 percent); woven $6 billion (up 4.8 percent); jute goods up 23.8 percent to $383 million; chemicals up 27.3 percent to $157 million; agriculture down 13.5 percent; frozen and live fish down 10.9 percent.
stories.figures: $17 billion exports (July-October); up 6 percent; knitwear $7.71 billion; woven $6 billion; garments about 80.4 percent of exports.

stories.headline: World Bank gives $450 million to strengthen Bangladesh's financial sector
stories.summary: Bangladesh signed a $450 million World Bank financing agreement — 328 million Special Drawing Rights — under the Financial Sector Support Project II to strengthen the financial sector's safety net, improve supervision and support banking reforms. Signed by ERD Secretary Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky and World Bank Director Jean Pesme, the project runs from July 2026 to June 2031, with a 25-year repayment term including a five-year grace period.
stories.why_it_matters: World Bank financing terms, SDRs and banking-sector reform are classic BCS/Bank topics; the figures and the people who signed are directly askable.
stories.exam_facts: Financing: $450 million (328 million SDR), Financial Sector Support Project II; signatories: Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky (ERD) and Jean Pesme (World Bank); project July 2026-June 2031; interest 1.5 percent; repayment 25 years, five-year grace; Bangladesh Bank implements under the Financial Institutions Division.
stories.exam_relevance: High — World Bank, SDR, banking reform.
stories.key_people: Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky, ERD Secretary; Jean Pesme, World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.
stories.figures: $450 million; 328 million SDR; 1.5 percent interest; 25-year repayment, five-year grace; project 1 July 2026-30 June 2031.

stories.headline: Remittance stays below $3 billion for a fifth straight month
stories.summary: Remittance stayed below $3 billion for a fifth straight month, with $2.87 billion arriving in October, up 12.1 percent year-on-year. Inflows have stayed under $3 billion since June, which bankers link to the war in the Middle East affecting expatriates' incomes. July-October inflows totalled $11.465 billion, up 13 percent, but import-payment pressure pushed the interbank dollar rate to Tk 124.30.
stories.why_it_matters: Remittance is Bangladesh's largest source of foreign exchange after exports; its level, trend and effect on the exchange rate are standard exam material.
stories.exam_facts: October remittance: $2.87 billion, up 12.1 percent year-on-year; below $3 billion since June (fifth straight month); July-October: $11.465 billion vs $10.149 billion a year earlier (up 13 percent); interbank rate Tk 124.30 per US dollar.
stories.exam_relevance: High — remittance, foreign exchange, exchange rate.
stories.figures: $2.87 billion in October; below $3 billion for five months; $11.465 billion in July-October; Tk 124.30 per US dollar.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank autonomy remains elusive amid IMF reform demands
stories.summary: Central bank autonomy remains elusive despite IMF pressure, as the Fund's $4.5 billion programme for Bangladesh — which included central bank independence among its conditions — was left by the government in May, eight months early, before a new package was sought. A draft amendment to the Bangladesh Bank Order 1972, prepared under former governor Ahsan H Mansur, remains pending, and the dual control of the central bank and the finance ministry continues.
stories.why_it_matters: Central bank independence is a core governance and economics topic for BCS/Bank, and the IMF programme conditions are directly askable.
stories.exam_facts: IMF $4.5 billion programme (2023) included central bank independence; government left it in May 2026, eight months early, and sought a new package; draft amendment to the Bangladesh Bank Order 1972 pending since the interim government; dual control by Bangladesh Bank and the Financial Institutions Division continues; Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury pledged to end dual control.
stories.key_people: Ahsan H Mansur, former Bangladesh Bank governor; Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance Minister; Ivo Krznar, IMF mission chief for Bangladesh; Arief Hossain Khan, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson.
stories.figures: $4.5 billion IMF programme; left eight months early (May 2026); Bangladesh Bank Order 1972.

stories.headline: CPD urges phasing out export cash incentives before 2029
stories.summary: The Centre for Policy Dialogue urged the government to set a timeline for phasing out export cash incentives and other LDC-only benefits before November 2029, after the UN General Assembly granted Bangladesh a three-year preparatory period before LDC graduation. CPD's Debapriya Bhattacharya warned the extension was exceptional and would not be repeated, and called for the Smooth Transition Strategy to be coordinated from the Prime Minister's Office with a public dashboard.
stories.why_it_matters: LDC graduation changes which trade benefits Bangladesh can keep; the phase-out timetable is a major exam topic in trade and economics.
stories.exam_facts: UNGA granted a three-year preparatory period; graduation now November 2029; UN Committee for Development Policy warned no further extension will be supported; CPD wants the Smooth Transition Strategy moved from the Economic Relations Division to the Prime Minister's Office, with parliamentary engagement and a public dashboard.
stories.exam_relevance: High — LDC graduation, WTO rules, trade policy.
stories.key_people: Debapriya Bhattacharya, CPD Distinguished Fellow; Nazneen Ahmed, CPD Executive Director.
stories.figures: Graduation November 2029 (three-year extension); phase out cash incentives before November 2029.

stories.headline: Bangla QR now allows person-to-person transfers
stories.summary: Person-to-person transfers through Bangla QR began on 1 November, letting people send money by scanning the recipient's QR code without typing a mobile or account number. Bangladesh Bank had directed banks, mobile financial services and payment providers to integrate the feature by 31 October. The central bank, which launched interoperable QR payments in 2023, aims to make 75 percent of transactions cashless by 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: Digital payments and financial inclusion are recurring BCS/Bank topics; Bangla QR is Bangladesh's own interoperable payment system.
stories.exam_facts: P2P transfers via Bangla QR from 1 November 2026; no mobile or account number needed, only a QR scan; banks, MFS providers, PSPs and PSOs told to integrate by 31 October; interoperable QR system launched 2023; target: 75 percent of transactions cashless by 2027.
stories.exam_relevance: High — digital payments, Bangladesh Bank, financial inclusion.
stories.figures: P2P from 1 November 2026; integration deadline 31 October; 75 percent cashless target by 2027; QR system launched 2023.

stories.headline: Bangladesh sets reform targets as LDC graduation delayed to 2029
stories.summary: Bangladesh submitted a time-bound reform roadmap to the EU and the UN after securing a three-year delay to LDC graduation, now set for 24 November 2029 instead of 24 November 2026. The roadmap, to be monitored annually, targets 7 percent GDP growth by 2029 from 4.14 percent in 2026 and inflation of 6 percent from 9.16 percent, with five ministries submitting monthly progress reports on banking, revenue and business-environment reforms.
stories.why_it_matters: LDC graduation is one of the biggest exam topics in Bangladesh's economy and foreign policy; the new date and the targets are directly askable.
stories.exam_facts: Graduation delayed to 24 November 2029 (from 24 November 2026) by a UN General Assembly decision adopted without a vote; roadmap targets 7 percent GDP growth by 2029 (from 4.14 percent in 2026) and 6 percent inflation (from 9.16 percent); EU and UN to monitor annually; five ministries to report monthly; EU is Bangladesh's largest export market.
stories.exam_relevance: High — LDC graduation, UN, EU, economic reform.
stories.key_people: Finance ministry official (source); Ireland spoke for the EU at the General Assembly.
stories.figures: Graduation 24 November 2029; GDP growth target 7 percent by 2029 (from 4.14 percent); inflation target 6 percent (from 9.16 percent).

stories.headline: Climate change cost Bangladesh $17.5 billion in lost earnings in 2025
stories.summary: Climate change cost Bangladesh an estimated $17.5 billion in lost earnings in 2025 through heat exposure alone, according to the 2026 Lancet Countdown report. Infants and people over 65 faced more than double the heatwave days of 1986-2005, and human-caused fine particulate pollution caused about 239,000 deaths in 2023. Bangladesh lost over 26 billion potential labour hours a year to heat in 2016-2025, 71 percent more than in the 1990s.
stories.why_it_matters: Climate and health figures are staple BCS/Bank general-knowledge material, and the Lancet Countdown is an authoritative source examiners cite.
stories.exam_facts: Heat exposure cost $17.5 billion in lost earnings in 2025; heatwave days for infants up 162 percent and for over-65s up 136 percent vs 1986-2005; PM2.5 pollution caused about 239,000 deaths in 2023; 26 billion potential labour hours lost a year to heat in 2016-2025; heat deaths among over-65s cost $3.8 billion a year in 2021-2025.
stories.exam_relevance: High — climate change, public health, Lancet Countdown.
stories.key_people: Shouro Dasgupta, environmental economist (keynote speaker); C3ER, BRAC University; Climate Change and Health Promotion Unit, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
stories.figures: $17.5 billion lost earnings in 2025; 239,000 PM2.5 deaths in 2023; 26 billion labour hours lost a year; $3.8 billion a year in heat deaths among over-65s.

stories.headline: Garment sector faces $4.8 billion shortfall in green investment
stories.summary: Bangladesh's garment sector faces a $4.8 billion shortfall against a $6.6 billion green-investment need for 2025-2029, with only $1.6 billion confirmed and $175 million in the pipeline, researchers told a Dhaka event organised by LightCastle Partners and Policy Exchange Bangladesh. Speakers said accessible green finance and simpler procedures are essential for smaller factories to cut emissions and stay competitive in global markets.

stories.key_people: Hasan Khaled Foisal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Finance.

stories.headline: Five men took part in journalist Alif's murder, Tajul fired the shot
stories.summary: Two accused in the murder of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif in Durgapur, Netrokona, told a court that five people took part in the killing and that Tajul Islam, the alleged mastermind, shot Alif with a pistol. Imran Islam and Sabbir Ahmed gave confessional statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Police say Tajul, who faces at least 13 cases, ran a border smuggling gang that Alif had exposed.

stories.exam_facts: Victim: journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif, Durgapur, Netrokona; confessional statements under Section 164 CrPC by Imran Islam (24) and Sabbir Ahmed (25) to Senior Judicial Magistrate Nurul Amin Bhuiyan; five people took part; Tajul Islam shot Alif; at least 13 cases against Tajul, including murder, arms, drugs and extortion.
stories.key_people: Tajul Islam (accused mastermind); Imran Islam and Sabbir Ahmed (accused); Nurul Amin Bhuiyan, Senior Judicial Magistrate, Durgapur; Khandaker Shaker Ahmed, OC, Durgapur Police Station.
stories.figures: Five people took part; at least 13 cases against Tajul; statements recorded 3:45pm-7pm on 1 November.

stories.headline: US Navy vessel USS Warrior arrives in Chattogram for CARAT-2026
stories.summary: The 68-metre US Navy vessel USS Warrior arrived at Chattogram Port on 1 November for CARAT-2026, the joint naval exercise with the Bangladesh Navy starting on 2 November. Led by Lieutenant Commander Mary Senoyuit, the ship will take part with a US P-8A aircraft and Bangladesh Navy ships and units under the SWADS Command. The exercise, focused on maritime security cooperation, ends when the vessel leaves on 5 November.

stories.headline: FBI says North Korea stole over $6 billion in crypto from Binance
stories.summary: The FBI accused North Korea of stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance on about 29 October, in what is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist. The North Korean group TraderTraitor, also blamed for a $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025, allegedly converted the assets into Ethereum for laundering. Binance said it set aside $6.34 billion in company funds and has replenished 90 percent of the loss.
stories.why_it_matters: Cybercrime, cryptocurrency and international security are growing exam topics; the scale makes this the largest crypto theft reported so far.
stories.exam_facts: Theft: over $6 billion from Binance, about 29 October 2026; accused group: TraderTraitor (North Korea-affiliated); same group blamed for $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025; Binance set aside $6.34 billion and replenished 90 percent; US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea's involvement.

stories.headline: Politics becoming a 'power-centric business model', says TIB
stories.summary: Transparency International Bangladesh said political participation in Bangladesh is becoming a 'power-centric business model', driven by abuse of power, black money and the criminalisation of politics. Launching a report on good governance in political parties, TIB executive director Iftekharuzzaman said the July uprising had raised hopes of ending power politics, but factionalism, opaque party financing and a lack of internal accountability have left political violence normalised.
stories.why_it_matters: Good governance, political party finance and corruption are core BCS topics; TIB's framing is a quotable assessment of the post-uprising political scene.
stories.exam_facts: Report: 'Institutional Good Governance in Bangladesh's Political Parties' (TIB); finding: political participation turning into a 'power-centric business model'; drivers: abuse of power, black money, criminalisation of politics; problems: opaque party financing, gap between reported and actual income/expenditure, weak internal democracy.
stories.key_people: Iftekharuzzaman, Executive Director, Transparency International Bangladesh.
stories.figures: Report launched 1 November 2026 at TIB office, Dhanmondi, Dhaka.

mcqs.question: The word 'mastermind' most nearly means:

options.C: The person who plans and directs a criminal activity

mcqs.explanation: A mastermind is the person who plans and directs a complicated or criminal activity.

mcqs.question: The phrase 'take to the streets' means:

mcqs.explanation: To take to the streets is to go out in public, usually to protest about something.

mcqs.question: The phrase 'cast doubt on' means:
mcqs.explanation: To cast doubt on something is to make people doubt whether it is true.

mcqs.question: According to BGMEA, how many garment factories were disrupted by the wage protests on 1 November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: BGMEA reported disruptions at 529 factories; 177 factories were shut in Savar and Ashulia, and 987,190 workers walked out.

mcqs.question: Who chairs the six-member wage board formed on 1 November 2026 for garment workers?
mcqs.explanation: Senior District and Sessions Judge Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman chairs the six-member wage board.

mcqs.question: What was the HSC pass rate in 2026?
mcqs.explanation: The HSC pass rate fell to 51.62 percent, a 22-year low; 57.12 percent was last year's rate, 61.07 percent was the Alim rate and 49.43 percent the technical rate.

mcqs.question: How many students secured GPA-5 in the HSC examinations in 2026?
mcqs.explanation: A total of 35,948 students secured GPA-5, down by 27,271 from 63,219 last year.

mcqs.question: How much did Bangladesh export in July-October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Exports grew 6 percent year-on-year to $17 billion in July-October; $7.71 billion was knitwear alone and $6 billion was woven garments.

mcqs.question: How much World Bank financing did Bangladesh sign for the financial sector on 30 October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Bangladesh signed a $450 million World Bank agreement (328 million SDR) under the Financial Sector Support Project II.

mcqs.question: How much remittance arrived in Bangladesh in October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: October remittance was $2.87 billion, up 12.1 percent year-on-year; $11.465 billion was the July-October total.

mcqs.question: The pending amendment for Bangladesh Bank autonomy concerns which law?
mcqs.explanation: A draft amendment to the Bangladesh Bank Order 1972, prepared under former governor Ahsan H Mansur, remains pending.

mcqs.question: By when does CPD want export cash incentives phased out?
mcqs.explanation: CPD urged the government to phase out export cash incentives and other LDC-only benefits before November 2029, when Bangladesh graduates from the LDC category.

mcqs.question: What do person-to-person transfers through Bangla QR let users do?

options.B: Send money by scanning a QR code without typing an account number

mcqs.explanation: P2P Bangla QR lets a person send money to another individual simply by scanning that person's QR code.

mcqs.question: When is Bangladesh now scheduled to graduate from the LDC category?
mcqs.explanation: The UN General Assembly extended the preparatory period to 24 November 2029, from 24 November 2026.

mcqs.question: How much did heat exposure cost Bangladesh in lost earnings in 2025, according to the Lancet Countdown report?
mcqs.explanation: Heat exposure alone caused an estimated $17.5 billion loss in potential earnings in 2025; $3.8 billion was the annual cost of heat deaths among over-65s.

mcqs.question: Which US Navy vessel arrived in Chattogram for the CARAT-2026 exercise?
mcqs.explanation: The 68-metre USS Warrior arrived at Chattogram Port on 1 November for CARAT-2026, led by Lieutenant Commander Mary Senoyuit.
